title: Ultrasound-Guided Investigation of the Interaction between PEEP, Venous Congestion, and Volume Responsiveness
summary:
Many critically ill patients in the intensive care unit need support with breathing from a ventilator. At the same time, their circulation has to be carefully monitored, for example to assess whether the heart is pumping enough blood through the body and whether the organs are receiving sufficient support.

Ultrasound examinations are often used for this purpose. However, it is not yet fully known whether different ventilator settings may influence the results of these examinations. The aim of this study is therefore to assess how reliable these ultrasound measurements are in ventilated patients.

Patients treated in the intensive care unit at University Hospital Regensburg may be included in the study if the study doctors consider participation possible based on the medical record and the patient’s current condition.

During a single study visit, ultrasound examinations will be performed. These examinations will assess how the heart is working and whether there are signs that fluid is backing up in the body. The measurements will be carried out at different ventilator settings.

In addition, the patient’s legs will be briefly raised. This causes more blood to temporarily flow back to the heart, allowing the study doctors to observe how the heart and circulation respond. No additional fluid will be given during this procedure.

The study visit is expected to take about 45 minutes. Afterwards, routine treatment will continue unchanged. The study will not prolong ventilation or the medication-induced sleep. During the further course of treatment, only data that are collected as part of routine care will be used.
conditions: venous congestion in the intensive care setting

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Admission to the intensive care unit
- Arterial blood pressure monitoring
- Invasive mechanical ventilation via endotracheal tube or tracheostomy tube
- Deep sedation (RASS −3 to −5)
Exclusion criteria:
- History of spontaneous pneumothorax
- Known pregnancy
- Pre-existing Child C liver cirrhosis
- Physical impairment, such as spinal instability, preventing passive leg raising
- Insufficient ultrasound accessibility for data acquisition
